original_question: An r-graph is an r-regular graph G such that every odd vertex set X subseteq V(G) is joined to its complement by at least r edges. Such a graph is poorly matchable if any two of its perfect matchings intersect. Is there a poorly matchable 5-edge-connected 5-graph?
target_in_paper: Problem 5.2 in Section 5 of arXiv:2411.10046: "Is there a poorly matchable 5-edge-connected 5-graph?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's target almost verbatim: it uses the same notions of an r-graph and a poorly matchable graph, specializes correctly to r=5, and asks the exact existence question stated as Problem 5.2.
missing_details: For a fully stand-alone statement, the graph model should be made explicit: in the source paper cited in Section 5, graphs are finite, may have parallel edges, and have no loops.
"Odd set" should be stated as "odd-cardinality vertex subset X of V(G)".
"5-edge-connected" should be defined explicitly as: for every nonempty proper subset Y of V(G), the edge-cut ∂G(Y) has size at least 5.
A "perfect matching" should be identified as a 1-factor.
"Any two perfect matchings intersect" should be clarified to mean they share at least one edge; equivalently, the graph has no two edge-disjoint perfect matchings.

If one wants the paper-faithful surrounding scope, this is the r=5 instance of the broader question about whether sufficiently highly edge-connected r-graphs must contain two disjoint perfect matchings; that motivation is implicit in your draft but explicit in the cited source.
refined_question: Does there exist a finite loopless graph G, possibly with parallel edges, such that G is 5-regular, every odd-cardinality vertex subset X of V(G) satisfies |∂G(X)| >= 5 (so G is a 5-graph), G is 5-edge-connected in the sense that |∂G(Y)| >= 5 for every nonempty proper subset Y of V(G), and every two perfect matchings of G share at least one edge?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if m(5) denotes the maximum integer t such that every 5-edge-connected 5-graph has t pairwise edge-disjoint perfect matchings, is m(5)=1?
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Problem 5.2 in Section 5 of arXiv:2411.10046, not the neighboring Problem 5.1 about 5-edge-connected 5-regular Class 2 graphs. Your draft already matches that target. The only refinements needed to make it fully stand-alone are to spell out the edge-connectivity condition, the graph model, and the meaning of intersection of perfect matchings. The broader m(r) framework and the relevance to Thomassen's question and the Fan-Raspaud conjecture come from the cited paper [1], but the workshop note itself asks the narrow existence question, so the refined version keeps that scope.
